# tokens: # Principle: List literals are inert at tokenize time; auto-evaluation
# happens later (at consume or end-of-Run).
# Per LANGREF.10.md ('Lists are quotation'):
#   'Square brackets create a list of *unevaluated* values. Words
#    inside a list are stored literally — they are not executed.'
# This is a property of the TOKENIZER / PARSER: `[ 1 addq 2 ]` produces
# a 3-element list `[Integer(1), Word(addq), Integer(2)]` that is NOT
# `[Integer(3)]`. Evaluation happens later via two engine passes:
#   (a) When the list is consumed as an argument to a word whose sig
#       does NOT mark that slot NoEvalArgs, execMatch runs autoEvalList
#       on the list before invoking the handler.
#   (b) When the list is residual on the stack at end-of-Run,
#       autoEvalStack drains it via autoEvalList.
# Both paths produce the SAME shape of output: a list whose contents
# are the residual stack of running the original elements through a
# fresh sub-engine.
# Rules being asserted
# 1. A bare list at end-of-Run auto-evaluates: `[1 addq 2]` → `[3]`.
# 2. A list consumed by a word with a `[List]` sig is auto-evaluated
#    BEFORE the handler sees it. So `lengthq [1 addq 2]` → 1 (the
#    auto-eval reduces to a 1-element list).
# 3. The `quote` word sets Quoted=true on a list, suppressing both
#    auto-eval paths. `lengthq quote [1 addq 2]` would expose the raw
#    3-element form — but in the spec subset `quote` paren-wrap is
#    needed (see autoeval.tsv for the wrapped forms).
# 4. Bare words never degrade to data. A list element that fails to
#    auto-evaluate — an undefined name, or a valid name dispatched
#    with the wrong arity — is an ERROR, in BOTH the consumed-arg
#    (execMatch) and end-of-Run (autoEvalStack) paths. So both
#    `lengthq [addq]` and `[addq]` alone error with signature_error.
#    To keep a word as literal data, use `foo/q` (atom) or `quote`
#    (a literal word list). This closed the silent-swallow footgun
#    that previously let a typo inside a consumed list pass through.
# 5. Lists inside lists are auto-evaluated recursively at end-of-Run
#    via the autoEvalStack drain (which calls autoEvalList per top-
#    level Eval list — but a subq-list inside a list element is
#    evaluated by the sub-engine running over the parent list's
#    elements, since the sub-engine is a full Run).
# Why this matters
# Auto-eval is the bridge from 'lists are data' to 'lists are code'.
# It removes the need for an explicit `do` in the common case while
# preserving the option to suppress (via `quote`).
# Auto-eval errors propagate uniformly (consumed and residual): a
# bare word is always a name to resolve, never a silent fallback to
# its literal token. The earlier execMatch swallow — a typo footgun
# that left the typo in the consumed list — was removed.
# === Test fixtures (defined in eng/go/spec_test.go::registerSpecWords) ===
#   addq     — [Number Number] forward-prec — args[1] + args[0] (decimal contagion)
#   firstq   — [List] forward-prec — first element or None for empty list
#   lengthq  — [List] forward-prec — list length as Integer
# === end fixtures ===
# 1. Bare list at end-of-Run auto-evaluates.
[ 1 addq 2 ]
note: auto-eval at end of Run reduces [1, addq, 2] to [3]
pure literals — auto-eval is a no-op

# tokens: [ ( 1 addq 2 ) ]
note: paren inside list — paren pre-evaluates to 3, list residue is [3]

# tokens: [ 1 addq 2 1 addq 3 ]
note: the body runs as ONE program: 1 addq 2 → 3 leaves [1,3]; second addq: forward 3 + stack top 3 → 6 (the 1 stays as residue). Result list is [1, 6]. Demonstrates that a 'list body' is a single program, not isolated expressions.
empty list — autoEvalList short-circuits

# tokens: # 2. Consumed list auto-evaluates BEFORE the handler.
lengthq [ 1 addq 2 ]
note: auto-eval [1 addq 2] → [3]; lengthq sees 1-element list

# tokens: firstq [ 1 addq 2 ]
note: auto-eval reduces; first returns the single element

# tokens: lengthq [ 1 2 3 ]
note: pure literals consume as-is

# tokens: # 4. Consumed-list auto-eval errors PROPAGATE (bare words never
# degrade to data — use foo/q or quote for literal word data).
lengthq [ addq ]
note: bare addq in body errors (0-arg, needs 2); propagates through lengthq

# tokens: lengthq [ undef_xyz ]
note: undefined word in body propagates — no silent fallback

# tokens: lengthq [ 1 addq ]
note: addq waits for forward args, none follow; insufficient-args error propagates

# tokens: # 5. Bare residual list errors propagate at end-of-Run (same as #4).
[ addq ]
note: bare list residual; autoEvalStack runs sub-engine; bare addq errors; propagates (same as the consumed-list path)

# tokens: [ 1 addq ]
note: bare list with insufficient args for inner addq — propagates

# tokens: [ unknown_xyz ]
note: undefined word in residual list propagates

# tokens: # 3. quote suppresses auto-eval. (Need paren wrap because quote is a
# function word — see autoeval.tsv for the rationale.)
lengthq ( quote [ 1 addq 2 ] )
note: quoted list keeps the 3 raw tokens

# tokens: firstq ( quote [ 1 addq 2 ] )
note: first element of the quoted list is the integer 1

# tokens: # 6. Nested lists at end-of-Run.
[ [ 1 addq 2 ] ]
note: outer list residual evaluates; inner list also evaluates (via sub-engine running over outer's elements)
pure-literal inner lists pass through

# tokens: # --- def binding and fn-param inertness (the binding-inertness contract) ---
# `def NAME [list]` evaluates the list VALUE at binding (like every plain
# arg slot); the reference then pushes inert data. A LIST passed to an fn
# param is quoted at frame binding ("treated as data values, not expanded
# as code bodies" — core_helpers.go), and the flag survives the return.
def b [ 1 2 ] b
note: plain def binds the evaluated list; the reference is inert data

# tokens: def b [ 1 2 ] b lengthq
note: the bound list is a data value the next word consumes

# tokens: def b [ 1 addq 2 ] b
note: the eval-list runs at def time and binds the collected [3]

# tokens: def b [ 1 2 ] b get 0
note: indexing the def-resolved list

# tokens: def b [ 1 2 ] do b
note: do splices the bound data list as a code body on request

# tokens: def f (fn [ [ x:List ] [ List ] [ x ] ]) f [ 1 2 ]
note: a list param is quoted at binding; the flag survives the return

# tokens: def f (fn [ [ x:List ] [ List ] [ x ] ]) (f [ 1 2 ]) lengthq
note: the quoted return is still a list value for the next word

# tokens: def f (fn [ [ x:Any ] [ Any ] [ x ] ]) f [ 1 2 ]
note: Any-typed params quote list args the same way

# tokens: def f (fn [ [ x:List ] [ Integer ] [ x lengthq ] ]) f [ 1 2 ]
note: the quoted param stays operable inside the body
